clue.text: Holiday site that's quiet by river

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge
P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

explanation.surface: A holiday spot beside a peaceful river.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a site of tents or cabins where people stay on holiday.

clue.text: Cathedral maps, about to be introduced

indicators.note: the about piece is introduced into the maps piece

parts.note: charts are maps, especially of seas
RE is Latin-derived for concerning, about

explanation.surface: Maps of a cathedral, with something about to be presented.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is the French city famous for its Gothic cathedral, standing for the building itself.

clue.text: Supper? Yours truly will have a litre!

parts.note: the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will drink a litre with supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is one example of a meal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See pram being resigned in lab units

indicators.note: read as re-signed, the letters are signed up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a pram being handed in, oddly, in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being resigned' is read as 're-signed': SEEPRAM written out again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperes are the standard units of electric current measured in a laboratory.

clue.text: Fall over in America

parts.note: the season Americans call fall has a different name on this side of the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles over while in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall over' looks like tumbling, but 'over in America' means 'over there': what they call the fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the season between summer and winter the fall.

clue.text: Pa's a listener out to make friendly conversation

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Dad is a good listener, out to chat amiably.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantries are polite remarks made in friendly small talk.

clue.text: Come back to gather fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Returning to pick the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back is to show up again after being gone.

clue.text: Get very wet, we hear, in this historic legal territory

indicators.note: we hear says the word is as it sounds when said

parts.note: to soak is to get drenched

explanation.surface: Getting drenched in an old jurisdiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A soke was a district under a lord's jurisdiction in medieval England.

clue.text: Can't memories get distorted in current accounts?

indicators.note: distorted means the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Bank current accounts so muddled you cannot remember them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current accounts' suggests banking, but means descriptions of events as they happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Commentaries are running descriptions of events while they are happening, such as sports broadcasts.

clue.text: Bit of praise with hit you don't see coming?

definitions.meaning: a congratulation, a small gesture of approval
a light slap delivered behind someone, out of their sight

explanation.surface: Praise offered alongside a blow from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for congratulation, and literally a tap on the rear of the body where it cannot be seen.

clue.text: Silent parent

definitions.meaning: saying nothing, as in 'keep quiet about it'
a mother, in British informal speech

explanation.surface: A parent who says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an idiom for keeping quiet and the British informal word for a mother.

clue.text: Dessert, but no starter? One might be fired!

indicators.note: the first letter of the dessert word is dropped, a starter being what comes first

parts.note: a trifle is a layered British pudding of sponge, custard, fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A meal served with pudding but no first course, and someone gets sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a menu course beside 'Dessert', but it is the first letter. A trifle is a British pudding of sponge, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun of this kind is something that is fired, a pun on being dismissed from a job.

clue.text: Chemical solution, sort put on a wrinkle mostly

parts.note: form is a kind or sort

indicators.note: mostly says the final letter of the wrinkle word is dropped

parts.note: a line is a wrinkle on the face

explanation.surface: A chemical solution applied to smooth out a wrinkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalin is a solution of formaldehyde in water, used as a preservative.

clue.text: As neighbour next door, one listening into home?

indicators.note: the listening piece goes inside the home piece

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An eavesdropping neighbour pressed to the wall of the house next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The house next door is the one closest to yours, the superlative of near.

clue.text: Foot-operated devices having lad steer awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy steering clumsily with pedals.
explanation.definitionFit: Treadles are levers worked by the foot, as on old sewing machines.

clue.text: Priests scattered fairies

indicators.note: the letters of the clergy word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Clergymen sent off in all directions by fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are small supernatural beings, elves or fairies of folklore.

clue.text: Second gate maybe for one keeps watch

parts.note: a gate is one example of an entry

explanation.surface: A second gate guarded by a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to stand guard.

clue.text: Cake that's part of breakfast or tea

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cake served at breakfast or at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'that's', which is only the link to 'part of'; the definition is 'Cake' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered gateau of central European origin.

clue.text: English bishop finds sin

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An English bishop discovers wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to go wrong, to do something mistaken or wicked.

clue.text: What person has a command to stop?

parts.note: who asks which person

explanation.surface: A question about who gave the order to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the call used to make a horse halt.

clue.text: Maiden inexperienced becomes upset, tender

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: M is a maiden, an over with no runs in cricket scoring
raw means green, untrained

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman grows distressed and sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over of six balls with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and tender are both synonyms for affectionate and kindly.

clue.text: Cash machine one of many appearing in Berlin in 1989?

definitions.meaning: British informal name for an ATM set in a bank's outer wall

definitions.text: one of many appearing in Berlin in 1989?
definitions.meaning: the Berlin Wall was breached in many places when it fell in 1989

explanation.surface: An ATM somehow linked to the fall of the Berlin Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names a street ATM this way, and literally the breaches knocked through the Berlin Wall in 1989 fit the phrase.

clue.text: Many set free, given pardon

indicators.note: the letters are set free to take a new order

explanation.surface: Many prisoners released after being pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon granted to offenders.

clue.text: In the morning getting bigger-than-average holy book

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon
OS is outsize, a clothing size larger than normal

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a large Bible first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament named after the prophet.
